questions.question: ____ is an example of required emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: Commercial motor vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What eliminates alcohol from the bloodstream?
questions.explanation: Your body processes alcohol at a fixed rate. Coffee and exercise cannot speed this up. Only time allows your body to remove alcohol naturally.

questions.question: If planning to change lanes, your mirrors should:

options.text: Be checked more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be checked more often than usual.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors regularly. When changing lanes, check them even more frequently to stay safe.

questions.question: Containers of hazardous materials must be:

options.text: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials containers must be braced so they do not fall, slide, or bounce during transport.

questions.question: How long should it take for oil pressure to reach a normal level when starting a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal level within seconds after starting the engine. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: Placards must be placed:

options.text: Within three inches of other markings.
So words or numbers are read from left to right.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words or numbers are read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least three inches away from other markings. They must be level so words and numbers read from left to right.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side or the other when used:

options.text: They will be the most effective.

questions.explanation: Brakes that pull to one side indicate a brake problem. Have them checked immediately.

questions.question: A Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives.

questions.question: You can find the identification numbers assigned to hazardous chemicals:

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
questions.explanation: The Department of Transportation Emergency Response Guide lists hazardous materials information and identification numbers.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should be:

options.text: Rubbing against other parts of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Exhaust system parts must be tight, not loose or broken. They should not rub against moving parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: When loading or unloading a tank divided by bulkheads, is equal weight distribution important?
questions.explanation: Tanks are often divided into smaller sections by bulkheads. When loading or unloading these tanks, distribute the weight evenly. Do not put too much weight on one end of the tank.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 of a hazardous materials shipping paper, what else must be included?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material.

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material.
questions.explanation: A "G" in Column 1 means the description in Column 2 is a generic name. A generic name must always include the technical name of the material.

questions.question: When can a commercial motor vehicle driver use a cell phone while driving?

options.text: Any time, with any cell phone.
Only with a hands-free cell phone, if allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only with a hands-free cell phone, if allowed.
questions.explanation: If you use a cell phone while driving a commercial vehicle, it must be hands-free and located close to you. However, any cell phone use while driving is distracting and dangerous. Know the cell phone laws in your state.

questions.question: On a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, at what air pressure will the valve pop out?
questions.explanation: An automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: Trailers built before what year are not required to have spring brakes?
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: When is hydroplaning most likely to happen?

options.text: When tire pressure is too low.
When tire tread is too deep.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tire pressure is too low.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens most often when driving on wet roads with low tire pressure and worn tire tread. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: If you must drive onto the shoulder in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Get both sets of wheels on the shoulder.
Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.
questions.explanation: If you drive onto the shoulder to avoid a hazard, stay there until you stop. Then signal, check your mirrors, and merge back into traffic. Do not brake hard on the shoulder at speeds above 20 mph. Keep one set of wheels on the pavement if you can.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is between three-quarters of a second and one second. At 55 mph, this means traveling about 61 feet before reacting.

questions.question: How can you identify a distracted driver?

options.text: They are focused on their cell phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are focused on their cell phone.
questions.explanation: A distracted driver may drift within their lane or cross lane lines; travel at changing speeds; use a cell phone, read a map, eat, or handle other items; or talk with passengers.

questions.question: If you must drive through flowing water or a large puddle, what should you do?

options.text: Try to stop in the water.

questions.explanation: Avoid driving through large puddles or moving water. If you must drive through water, slow down, shift to a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. This keeps water and mud out of the brake mechanisms.
